nodes.description: Enamel maturation requires cyclic acidification of the enamel organ so that matrix proteins are removed and hydroxyapatite crystals can grow. Rogdi-null mouse incisors show no cyclic acidification, reduced expression of the enamel matrix genes Enam, Amelx and Ambn, and altered expression of V-ATPase-interacting genes (Wdr72, Slc9a3r2, Atp6v0c).

nodes.description: Rogdi mutant flies sleep poorly because metabotropic GABA transmission onto wake-promoting dopaminergic neurons is reduced. The study proposes that a similar loss of GABAergic inhibition could underlie seizures in KTS; this has not been tested in a vertebrate model.

Seizures begin in infancy or early childhood (in the Druze cohort between six and twelve months) and are often resistant to antiseizure medication; super-refractory status epilepticus has been reported. Seizure severity tracks the pace of cognitive and motor deterioration.

nodes.description: ROGDI is the human homolog of yeast Rav2 and binds the N-terminal domains of both Rabconnectin-3 alpha (DMXL1/DMXL2) and beta (WDR7), probably bridging the two subunits. Rabconnectin-3 drives reassociation of the V1 and V0 sectors of the V-ATPase, which reactivates proton pumping and organelle acidification. Loss of ROGDI is therefore expected to reduce V-ATPase assembly; this has been shown by complementation in yeast and by interaction studies, not yet by direct measurement in patient cells.

evidence.reference_title: The ROGDI protein mutated in Kohlschutter-Tonz syndrome is a novel subunit of the Rabconnectin-3 complex implicated in V-ATPase assembly.
evidence.snippet: ROGDI shares extensive structural homology with yeast Rav2 and can functionally replace Rav2 in yeast.

evidence.reference_title: The ROGDI protein mutated in Kohlschutter-Tonz syndrome is a novel subunit of the Rabconnectin-3 complex implicated in V-ATPase assembly.
evidence.snippet: ROGDI binds to the N-terminal domains of both Rabconnectin-3 α and β, similar to Rav2 binding to Rav1.

nodes.description: ROGDI is enriched at presynaptic sites, where it colocalizes with Bassoon and synaptic vesicle markers. Synaptic vesicles are loaded with neurotransmitter using the proton gradient generated by the V-ATPase, so loss of ROGDI is proposed to impair vesicle acidification and transmitter release. Rogdi-null mice have a lowered seizure threshold, hyperactivity and memory deficits. The precise synaptic defect has not been measured, and brain MRI is often normal early in the disease.

nodes.description: Biallelic nonsense, frameshift, splice-site and intragenic deletion variants abolish ROGDI protein. Most variants are expected to trigger nonsense-mediated decay or to disrupt the four-helix bundle that holds the protein's alpha domain together; the first missense variant was reported only in 2025, in trans to a frameshift.
